newsitem.title: UK: Ad agency chilled by Haagen-Dazs new pitch request.
newsitem.headline: Ad agency chilled by Haagen-Dazs new pitch request.

text.p: London-based advertising agency Bartle Bogle Hegarty declined comment on Wednesday on why it would not re-pitch for Haagen-Dazs ice cream's European advertising account, but industry sources said BBH felt it merited better treatment by the ice cream brand's parent company.

Pillsbury Europe, a unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, earlier had said it would conduct a full-service pitch review of the Haagen-Dazs advertising account. Pillsbury had said it hoped that BBH, creator of ads for Haagen-Dazs emphasising its sensual pleasures, would participate in the review.

But after six years of successfully handling the Haagen-Dazs account, BBH believed Pillsbury Europe should have first asked it to address the company's new brief and proceeded to open it up for a full-scale review only if it was not happy with BBH's proposal, industry sources said.
"BBH pitched and won in 1989, re-pitched in '92 and '94," one source told Reuters. "It's not right for a successful agency to re-pitch for the fourth time in six years."
BBH on Wednesday said it had chosen not to participate and said its Motive Communications unit, responsible for media planning and buying, would also not take part in the pitch review.

"BBH is very proud of the world-famous advertising we have developed for Haagen-Dazs," BBH group director Julian Martin said. "It is now used by Pillsbury in Asia as well as Europe. We wish them well with their future agency."
Martin declined to comment further on the decision.

BBH won the Haagen-Dazs advertising account in Britain in 1990 and launched its "seriously sensual" press ads for the ice cream in 1991. Sales of Haagen-Dazs leaped 398 percent in 1991 over 1990 levels.
BBH pitched and won the pan-European advertising account for Haagen-Dazs in 1992 and again in 1994.
BBH said the enormous brand awareness created by its Haagen-Dazs ad campaign has been built on a UK media spend of 4.5 million pounds ($7.3 million).

But although Pillsbury has scooped up sales in Europe since the 1991 launch of the Haagen-Dazs ads, profits have failed to follow. For the financial year ended September 30, 1996, Grand Met reported that in Europe Haagen-Dazs' "local currency results improved to almost break even."

Pillsbury's decision to put the Haagen-Dazs account up for review follows the introduction of a new European brand management structure for Pillsbury's four brands, including Haagen-Dazs, Old El Paso, Green Giant and Pillsbury.

Pillsbury UK managing director Martin Jamieson has said the company is looking to promote the ice cream brand with a single ad campaign across Europe. Pillsbury officials could not be reached for comment on the decision to put the Haagen-Dazs account up for review. A spokeswoman said the company would not disclose the advertising agencies pitching for the account.
